references.text: Isaiah uses the same phrasing 'that you may believe that I am' (Hebrew: ki ani hu) as a direct claim to God's divine identity and foreknowledge of events before they occur.
Here God confirms his eternal existence and ability to predict the future with the words 'I am', which is central to Jesus' statement in John 13:19.
God proclaims that he announces the future before it happens ('from the beginning'), so that people may believe that he is the only true God, a theme reflected in Jesus' words to his disciples.
God says that he has announced earlier things before they happened, so that no one would say their gods did it, but rather 'I am' who controls history.

Jesus' statement 'when you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am' (literally 'that I am he') is a direct parallel to the expression in 13:19, where knowledge of the event leads to belief in his identity.
